candidates: When writing conditions that detect a wildcard-bind host (e.g., to set `allowedHosts = true` or skip host validation), check both the IPv4 wildcard `'0.0.0.0'` AND the IPv6 wildcard `'::'`. Checking only `'0.0.0.0'` will silently leave IPv6 wildcard-bound servers subject to host rejection.

In `build-dev.ts` (and any other file that calls `presets.apply('core', {})` more than once), values destructured from an early preset pass—such as `allowedHosts`—can become stale after subsequent preset reloads that incorporate builder or renderer presets. Always re-read or re-destructure `core.*` values from the final preset pass before using them in startup warnings or output messages.

When adding any logging call (e.g., `logger.warn(...)`) in a file that previously only imported other named exports from `@storybook/core/node-logger` (e.g., `deprecate`), explicitly add `logger` to the named import list. The logger is not globally available and omitting it causes a build/type-check failure.

When constructing a `URL` from a potentially-relative path using a variable base (e.g., `new URL(request.url, options.localAddress)`), always provide a safe fallback when the base may be `undefined` (e.g., `options.localAddress ?? 'http://localhost'`). HTTP upgrade `request.url` values are typically relative, so an undefined base will throw and can silently reject valid WebSocket connections with a 403.

Changelog entries for security-related changes must be sufficiently descriptive: state exactly what validation was added (e.g., host/origin validation for HTTP requests and WebSocket connections), describe the behavioral impact (e.g., external hostnames such as ngrok URLs may now be blocked), and name the configuration option users must set to restore access (e.g., `core.allowedHosts` in `main.ts`).
